test_objective: Verify that an authenticated user can change their email address only after entering a valid new email address and successfully verifying it with the correct one-time code.
scope: Authenticated user enters a new email address.
System sends a verification code to the new email address.
System updates email only after the correct code is entered.
Invalid, empty, malformed, boundary, duplicate, retry, navigation, refresh, session-expiry, authorization, and state-consistency checks where relevant.
risks: Email may be updated before verification.
Invalid or malformed email addresses may pass validation.
Verification code may be sent to the wrong address.
Incorrect code entry may still update the email.
Duplicate submissions may create inconsistent state.
Refresh, navigation, or session expiry may leave pending state unclear.
Unauthorized users may access or abuse the email-change flow.
Missing code expiry, retry, resend, and rate-limit rules may cause inconsistent implementation and testing ambiguity.
clarifications_needed: What exact email validation rules should be used?
Are internationalized email addresses supported?
Are plus-addressing, subdomains, uppercase characters, and long TLDs allowed?
What are the minimum and maximum allowed email lengths?
Can the new email be the same as the current email?
Can the new email already belong to another account?
How long is the one-time code valid?
What is the required code format and length?
What happens after multiple incorrect code attempts?
Is there a resend verification code option?
If multiple codes are requested, are previous codes invalidated?
What should happen if the user refreshes or navigates away during verification?
What should happen if the session expires during the flow?
Should the old email receive a notification?
Should the new email receive confirmation after successful update?
Are there rate limits for email-change requests or code submissions?
Should audit logs be created for email-change attempts and successful updates?
What exact error messages should be displayed?
Should email comparison be case-sensitive or normalized?
What should happen if sending the verification code fails?

test_cases.Title: Change email with valid new email and correct verification code
test_cases.Preconditions: User is authenticated and has access to the email-change flow.
Steps: Enter a valid new email address.
Submit the email-change request.
Retrieve the verification code from the new email address.
Enter the correct verification code.
Submit verification.
test_cases.Expected Result: Verification code is sent to the new email address, and the account email is updated only after the correct code is submitted.

test_cases.Title: Verification code is sent to the entered new email address
test_cases.Preconditions: User is authenticated.
Steps: Enter a valid new email address.
Submit the email-change request.
Check the inbox for the new email address.
test_cases.Expected Result: Verification code is delivered to the new email address.

test_cases.Title: Email remains unchanged after valid email submission but before code verification
test_cases.Preconditions: User is authenticated and has an existing account email.
Steps: Enter a valid new email address.
Submit the email-change request.
Do not enter the verification code.
Check the current account email value.
test_cases.Expected Result: Account email remains unchanged until the correct verification code is entered.

test_cases.Title: Email format accepted for common valid email structure
test_cases.Preconditions: User is authenticated.
Steps: Enter an email address using a common valid structure, such as local-part, @ symbol, domain, and TLD.
Submit the email-change request.
test_cases.Expected Result: System accepts the valid email format and proceeds to send a verification code.

test_cases.Title: Correct verification code updates only to the requested new email
test_cases.Preconditions: User is authenticated and has requested an email change.
Steps: Submit a valid new email address.
Receive the verification code.
Enter the correct verification code.
Confirm the updated account email.
test_cases.Expected Result: Account email is updated to the same new email address used for the verification request.
test_cases.Notes: Prevents mismatch between requested and updated email.

test_cases.Title: Empty email address is rejected
test_cases.Preconditions: User is authenticated.
Steps: Leave the new email field empty.
Submit the email-change request.
test_cases.Expected Result: System rejects the request, does not send a verification code, and does not update the account email.

test_cases.Title: Malformed email without @ symbol is rejected
test_cases.Preconditions: User is authenticated.
Steps: Enter a malformed email address without an @ symbol.
Submit the request.
test_cases.Expected Result: System rejects the email format, does not send a verification code, and does not update the account email.

test_cases.Title: Malformed email without domain is rejected
test_cases.Preconditions: User is authenticated.
Steps: Enter an email address missing the domain portion.
Submit the request.
test_cases.Expected Result: System rejects the email format, does not send a verification code, and does not update the account email.

test_cases.Title: Malformed email without local part is rejected
test_cases.Preconditions: User is authenticated.
Steps: Enter an email address missing the local part before @.
Submit the request.
test_cases.Expected Result: System rejects the email format, does not send a verification code, and does not update the account email.

test_cases.Title: Incorrect verification code does not update email
test_cases.Preconditions: User is authenticated and has requested an email change with a valid new email.
Steps: Enter an incorrect verification code.
Submit verification.
Check the account email.
test_cases.Expected Result: System rejects the incorrect code and keeps the original account email unchanged.

test_cases.Title: Empty verification code is rejected
test_cases.Preconditions: User is authenticated and has requested an email change.
Steps: Leave the verification code field empty.
Submit verification.
test_cases.Expected Result: System rejects the empty code and does not update the account email.

test_cases.Title: Malformed verification code is rejected
test_cases.Preconditions: User is authenticated and has requested an email change.
Steps: Enter a verification code that does not match the required code format.
Submit verification.
test_cases.Expected Result: System rejects the malformed code and does not update the account email.

test_cases.Title: Duplicate email-change submission does not update email prematurely
test_cases.Preconditions: User is authenticated.
Steps: Enter a valid new email address.
Submit the request multiple times quickly.
Do not enter any verification code.
Check account email.
test_cases.Expected Result: Account email remains unchanged until correct verification code entry.
test_cases.Notes: Expected code-generation behavior for duplicates needs clarification.

test_cases.Title: Verification code sending failure does not update account email
test_cases.Preconditions: User is authenticated and verification email sending can be simulated as failed.
Steps: Enter a valid new email address.
Submit the request while code delivery fails.
Check account email.
test_cases.Expected Result: Account email is not updated if the verification code is not successfully sent.

test_cases.Title: Minimum valid email length is handled according to validation rules
test_cases.Preconditions: User is authenticated.
Steps: Enter an email address at the minimum valid length allowed by the system.
Submit the request.
test_cases.Expected Result: System handles the boundary value according to defined email validation rules and does not update email before verification.

test_cases.Title: Maximum valid email length is handled according to validation rules
test_cases.Preconditions: User is authenticated.
Steps: Enter an email address at the maximum valid length allowed by the system.
Submit the request.
test_cases.Expected Result: System handles the boundary value according to defined email validation rules and does not update email before verification.

test_cases.Title: Email exceeding maximum allowed length is rejected
test_cases.Preconditions: User is authenticated.
Steps: Enter an email address longer than the maximum allowed length.
Submit the request.
test_cases.Expected Result: System rejects the email, does not send a verification code, and does not update the account email.

test_cases.Title: Verification code length boundary is handled according to code rules
test_cases.Preconditions: User is authenticated and has requested an email change.
Steps: Enter a code shorter than the required length.
Submit verification.
Enter a code longer than the required length.
Submit verification.
test_cases.Expected Result: System rejects codes that do not match the required code length and does not update the account email.

test_cases.Title: Verification code retry limit boundary is handled consistently
test_cases.Preconditions: User is authenticated and has requested an email change.
Steps: Enter incorrect verification codes up to the configured retry limit.
Attempt one additional incorrect submission.
test_cases.Expected Result: System behaves according to the configured retry-limit rules and does not update the account email without the correct code.

test_cases.Title: Refresh page after email submission before verification
test_cases.Preconditions: User is authenticated and has submitted a valid new email address.
Steps: Refresh the page before entering the verification code.
Continue or revisit the verification flow as supported.
Check the account email.
test_cases.Expected Result: Account email remains unchanged until the correct verification code is entered.
test_cases.Notes: Expected pending-state behavior after refresh needs clarification.

test_cases.Title: Navigate away after email submission before verification
test_cases.Preconditions: User is authenticated and has submitted a valid new email address.
Steps: Navigate away from the verification step before entering the code.
Return to the email-change flow.
Check account email.
test_cases.Expected Result: Account email remains unchanged until the correct verification code is entered.
test_cases.Notes: Expected pending-state behavior after navigation needs clarification.

test_cases.Title: Session expires before verification code is submitted
test_cases.Preconditions: User is authenticated and has submitted a valid new email address.
Steps: Allow or simulate session expiry before entering the verification code.
Attempt to submit the code.
Check account email.
test_cases.Expected Result: System does not update the email unless the user is authenticated and the correct code is accepted according to session rules.

test_cases.Title: Retry with correct code after an incorrect code attempt
test_cases.Preconditions: User is authenticated and has requested an email change.
Steps: Enter an incorrect verification code.
Submit verification.
Enter the correct verification code.
Submit verification.
test_cases.Expected Result: Email remains unchanged after the incorrect code; subsequent behavior follows retry rules, and email updates only if the correct code is accepted.

test_cases.Title: Submit two different new email addresses before verification
test_cases.Preconditions: User is authenticated.
Steps: Submit a valid first new email address.
Before verifying, submit a different valid new email address.
Use the verification code from the first email, if available.
Check account email.
test_cases.Expected Result: Email is not updated unless the correct code for the active pending email-change request is entered.

test_cases.Title: Duplicate verification-code submission after successful update
test_cases.Preconditions: User is authenticated and has successfully updated the email using the correct code.
Steps: Submit the same verification code again, if the UI or API allows.
Check account email.
test_cases.Expected Result: Account state remains consistent and is not incorrectly changed by duplicate submission.
test_cases.Notes: Post-success code reuse rules need clarification.

test_cases.Title: Same email address as current account email
test_cases.Preconditions: User is authenticated and knows the current account email.
Steps: Enter the current account email as the new email.
Submit the request.
test_cases.Expected Result: System handles the same-email submission according to product rules and does not create an inconsistent account state.

test_cases.Title: New email address already used by another account
test_cases.Preconditions: User is authenticated and an email already associated with another account exists.
Steps: Enter the email address already associated with another account.
Submit the request.
test_cases.Expected Result: System handles the duplicate email according to product rules and does not update the account incorrectly.

test_cases.Title: Unauthenticated user cannot access email-change flow
test_cases.Preconditions: User is not authenticated.
Steps: Attempt to access the email-change flow.
test_cases.Expected Result: Unauthenticated user cannot change an account email.
test_cases.Notes: Authentication is required by the user story.

test_cases.Title: Email is not updated without verification code
test_cases.Preconditions: User is authenticated.
Steps: Submit a valid new email address.
Attempt to complete or bypass the flow without entering a code.
Check account email.
test_cases.Expected Result: Account email remains unchanged without the correct verification code.

test_cases.Title: Email is not updated with code for another pending request
test_cases.Preconditions: User is authenticated and multiple pending email-change attempts can be created.
Steps: Submit one valid new email address.
Submit a second valid new email address.
Attempt verification using the code from the non-active or unrelated request.
test_cases.Expected Result: Account email is not updated unless the correct code for the intended active request is entered.

test_cases.Title: Verification code cannot be reused after successful email update
test_cases.Preconditions: User has completed an email change using a valid code.
Steps: Attempt to reuse the same code for another submission.
test_cases.Expected Result: Reuse does not cause unauthorized or duplicate email changes; account state remains consistent.

test_cases.Title: Rate limiting or abuse prevention for repeated code submissions
test_cases.Preconditions: User is authenticated and has a pending email-change request.
Steps: Submit repeated incorrect verification codes.
test_cases.Expected Result: System handles repeated attempts according to defined abuse-prevention rules and never updates the email without the correct code.
test_cases.Notes: Rate limiting and lockout rules need clarification.

exploratory_charters: Explore email format validation using a broad set of valid-looking and invalid-looking emails to identify gaps between expected and actual validation.
Explore state transitions across email submission, verification pending, successful verification, failed verification, refresh, navigation, and re-login.
Explore duplicate and rapid submissions for both new email entry and verification code entry.
Explore behavior when multiple email-change requests are initiated before any verification is completed.
Explore session changes during the flow, including logout, session expiry, and login from another session if applicable.
Explore security bypass attempts where email update is attempted before or without correct code verification.
Explore verification email content and destination to confirm the code is sent to the new email address only.
coverage_gaps: Exact email validation specification is missing.
Verification code length, format, expiration, retry, and reuse rules are missing.
Duplicate pending-request behavior is not defined.
Current-email and already-used-email behavior is not defined.
Rate limiting and lockout requirements are not defined.
Notification requirements to old or new email are not defined.
Code delivery failure behavior is not defined.
recommendation: Proceed with testing the core acceptance criteria first: valid email entry, email-format validation, code delivery to the new email, and update only after correct code entry. Before final sign-off, clarify validation rules, code lifecycle rules, duplicate-request behavior, session-expiry behavior, and security controls because these directly affect test completeness and account-security risk.
